bug_description.original:
Detailed report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=5617496443846656

Project: harfbuzz
Fuzzer: libFuzzer_harfbuzz_hb-fuzzer
Fuzz target binary: hb-fuzzer
Job Type: libfuzzer_msan_harfbuzz
Platform Id: linux

Crash Type: Use-of-uninitialized-value
Crash State:
  hb_buffer_t::set_cluster
  hb_buffer_t::merge_out_clusters
  reorder_marks_arabic

Sanitizer: memory (MSAN)

Reproducer Testcase: https://oss-fuzz.com/download?testcase_id=5617496443846656
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01's saved run reproduces `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` in `hb_buffer_t::set_cluster()` during the second `hb_shape()` call at `test/fuzzing/hb-fuzzer.cc:30`, the branch that shapes the last 64 bytes of the exact staged witness as `text32[16]`. `hb_buffer_add_utf32()` first grows the glyph-info array with `hb_buffer_t::enlarge()`, whose `realloc()` leaves spare old-`info` capacity uninitialized. During `_hb_ot_shape_normalize()`, the first decomposition round writes normalized output under `clear_output()` and then `swap_buffers()` makes that decomposed sequence the live `info` array while leaving the pre-decomposition allocation as inactive `out_info`. In the second normalization round, `reorder_marks_arabic()` computes a non-empty live mark span `[i, j)` but mistakenly calls `merge_out_clusters(start, j)` before its in-place `memmove()` reordering. That helper is only correct while an output buffer is active; here it reuses current live indices to read `out_info[start..j)`, derives `cluster` from stale pre-decomposition entries, and then calls `set_cluster(out_info[i], cluster)` on the same stale range. The branch `if (info.cluster != cluster)` in `set_cluster()` therefore reads an uninitialized `cluster` field from stale `out_info`, matching the saved MSAN stack `set_cluster -> merge_out_clusters -> reorder_marks_arabic`. The fixing commit changes the call site to `merge_clusters(start, j)`, keeping cluster merging on the live `info` array.

source.description: First project-code statement on the witnessed crash path that admits the attacker-controlled UTF-32 tail bytes into HarfBuzz's shaping buffer.
source.value_from: The exact staged `poc` is 195 bytes long, so the harness's second branch runs, copies the last 64 bytes into `text32[16]`, and calls `hb_buffer_add_utf32()` at `test/fuzzing/hb-fuzzer.cc:28`. This wrapper is the first project statement that forwards those 16 attacker-controlled UTF-32 codepoints into the internal add/normalize pipeline later reaching `reorder_marks_arabic()`.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSan crash site. `set_cluster()` branches on the stale `out_info[i].cluster` field passed through `merge_out_clusters()`, and that field is uninitialized on the witnessed path.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and the saved vulnerable run log report `MemorySanitizer: use-of-uninitialized-value` at `src/hb-buffer-private.hh:298:9` with top stack `hb_buffer_t::set_cluster -> hb_buffer_t::merge_out_clusters -> reorder_marks_arabic`.

root_cause.description: The Arabic second-round reorder is operating in place on the live `info` array after normalization, but it calls the out-buffer helper `merge_out_clusters()` instead of `merge_clusters()`. That sends current live indices into the inactive stale `out_info` array.
root_cause.note: The fixing commit changes this exact line to `buffer->merge_clusters (start, j);`. In `_hb_ot_shape_normalize()`, `reorder_marks_arabic()` is called in the second "reorder (inplace)" round after the first round already executed `buffer->swap_buffers()`, so `have_output` is false and cluster merging must stay on live `info`.

parser_admitted.note: The authoritative Stage 01 crash stack reaches `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` at line 30, the second shaping call after line 28 populated the buffer from the witness tail with `hb_buffer_add_utf32()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSan attributes the poisoned bytes to this heap reallocation of the old `info` buffer. Only the live entries later written by `hb_buffer_t::add()` are initialized; spare capacity in the old pre-decomposition allocation remains indeterminate and later becomes stale `out_info` after `swap_buffers()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The saved origin stack is `realloc -> hb_buffer_t::enlarge -> hb_buffer_t::ensure -> hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf32_t<true>> -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 28, matching the UTF-32 ingestion path for the second harness branch.

fine_trace.note: Source. On the witnessed path, the harness's second branch copies the last 64 bytes of the exact staged `poc` into `text32[16]` and enters HarfBuzz here at `test/fuzzing/hb-fuzzer.cc:28`. This wrapper starts the internal UTF-32 ingestion that both allocates the later stale `info` buffer and materializes the live codepoints subsequently normalized and reordered.

Uninitialized-value origin. During step 1's `hb_buffer_add_utf32()` call, `hb_buffer_add_utf` first calls `ensure()` for the 16-codepoint UTF-32 input and reaches this `realloc()`. The grown old-`info` allocation contains spare capacity beyond the live entries, and `realloc()` does not initialize that tail; MSAN reports the later poisoned value as originating here.

fine_trace.code:
next = utf_t::next (next, end, &u, replacement);
buffer->add (u, old_next - (const T *) text);
fine_trace.note: The UTF-32 ingestion loop decodes each attacker-controlled `text32` element and passes its array offset as the glyph `cluster`. Inside `hb_buffer_t::add()` at lines 255-269, HarfBuzz zeroes only the current live slot before writing `codepoint` and `cluster`, so the original live prefix is initialized but the spare tail from step 2 remains untouched.

After the first normalization round has emitted decomposed glyphs to the output buffer under `clear_output()` / `decompose_cluster()`, this call makes that decomposed sequence the live `info` array. Because the saved MSAN read later comes from stale pre-decomposition storage, the witness necessarily reached the swapped-buffer state where the old allocation from steps 2-3 became inactive `out_info` while the current live `info` sequence had already moved past the old initialized prefix.

In the second normalization round, Arabic mark reordering scans the live decomposed `info` array and finds a non-empty mark run `[i, j)` to shift. The `if (i == j) continue;` guard is not taken on the crash path, so the cluster-merge call at line 679 executes with `start` as the base boundary and `j` as the exclusive end of the mark run.

Root cause. `reorder_marks_arabic()` is shifting the live `info` array in place, but it invokes the out-buffer-only helper `merge_out_clusters()` instead of `merge_clusters()`. The fix changes exactly this call, because after step 4 the current glyphs live in `info` while `out_info` is only the stale pre-decomposition buffer.

Instead of reading clusters from live `info[start..j)`, the wrong helper derives `cluster` by scanning stale `out_info[start..end)`. For the current indices supplied by step 6, at least one of those stale entries lies in the untouched tail of the old allocation from step 2, so this step materializes the uninitialized `cluster` value later carried into `set_cluster()`.

fine_trace.code:
for (unsigned int i = start; i < end; i++)
  set_cluster (out_info[i], cluster);
fine_trace.note: The helper then iterates the same stale range and passes each stale `out_info[i]` together with the derived `cluster` into `set_cluster()`. This is the direct propagation from the stale-buffer read in step 7 to the crashing helper.

Sink. Here `info` is the stale `out_info[i]` reference from step 8, so `info.cluster` reads the uninitialized cluster field from the old pre-decomposition buffer and branches on it against step 7's derived `cluster`. MemorySanitizer reports `use-of-uninitialized-value` at this exact branch with the saved stack `set_cluster -> merge_out_clusters -> reorder_marks_arabic`.

allocation_context.description: The saved MSAN origin stack attributes the poisoned bytes to the `info`-buffer `realloc()`. That allocation is not itself the logical bug; it becomes observable because `reorder_marks_arabic()` later indexes stale `out_info` entries that were never initialized after the original live prefix.

allocation_stack.function: void hb_buffer_add_utf<hb_utf32_t<true> >(hb_buffer_t*, hb_utf32_t<true>::codepoint_t const*, int, unsigned int, int)

cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. The allocation context explains why the old pre-decomposition `info` tail is uninitialized, and the root cause at `reorder_marks_arabic()` is exactly what misroutes current live indices into that stale allocation.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack is `set_cluster -> merge_out_clusters -> reorder_marks_arabic -> _hb_ot_shape_normalize -> ... -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` line 30, and the fine trace covers the UTF-32 ingestion, stale-buffer swap state, wrong helper call, stale cluster read, and final branch sink.

format.name: HarfBuzz hb-fuzzer blob
format.contract: The staged witness is the exact 195-byte file `poc`. In the authoritative Stage 01 run, `hb-fuzzer` uses the whole blob as the font data for `hb_blob_create()` / `hb_face_create()`, copies its last 64 bytes into `text32[16]`, and the second `hb_shape()` call at `test/fuzzing/hb-fuzzer.cc:30` reaches Arabic normalization's in-place mark-reorder path where `reorder_marks_arabic()` calls `merge_out_clusters(start, j)`. The available artifacts only establish this exact font-plus-trailing-UTF-32 witness and do not justify a broader trigger class.
